category_title: Students who disengage and exhibit behavioral issues when curriculum lacks challenge and teacher communication is perceived as indirect
student_description: Raheem is a capable student who quickly disengages and develops an 'I don't care' attitude when faced with unchallenging review, overly complex explanations, or inconsistent discipline. He uniquely needs straightforward, jargon-free instruction, continuous and escalating academic challenges, and fair, consistent boundaries to maintain his respect and engagement.

criteria.rationale: Raheem perceives complex academic language as 'beating around the bush' and becomes frustrated, preferring instruction that gets straight to the point.
criteria.check: The tutor uses plain, straightforward language to explain concepts, actively avoiding unnecessary academic jargon or overly complex phrasing.

criteria.rationale: Raheem disengages and develops an 'I don't care' attitude when forced to sit through review of concepts he already knows.
criteria.check: The tutor acknowledges Raheem's current understanding and offers an immediate opportunity to advance, tackle a harder problem, or receive one-on-one extension rather than forcing him to complete basic review.

criteria.rationale: Raheem complains when instruction is dry and 'playing with words,' needing engaging delivery to maintain his interest.
criteria.check: The tutor incorporates an engaging element—such as a real-world hook, conversational tone, or interactive challenge—rather than delivering a dry, rote explanation.
